raw_response:
I’m 57 now, and with only part of the family available on the farm, I won’t spread myself too thin this year. I’ll keep most of my land in cotton because that’s what I know well and it usually brings cash, but I’ll still keep some land in wheat-maize so we have grain and not all our income depends on cotton price. I’ll do it the way people around here usually do, with only small changes. For wheat, I already know if I save too much on fertilizer, the leaves turn weak and yield falls, so I’ll still feed it enough and give 3 irrigations if the spring is dry. After wheat harvest, maize has to go in fast, so I won’t do heavy tillage there, just a quick turnover and sow right away. Cotton needs more watching and more hand work, so I won’t plant the whole 14 mu with it. I’ll use well water when needed, but pumping costs money, so I’ll not irrigate unless the field is really dry. I’d rather spend a bit more on fertilizer and seed than risk a bad harvest, but I still have to leave cash in hand because some family members work away and farm labor at home is not steady.
